prompt:
Use $text-composition in fiction-drafting mode from .agents/skills/text-composition/SKILL.md.

Write the complete original story specified in inputs/planning.md. Keep it entirely in four receipts, with annotations carrying the story and no external narrator. Target 220–320 words of story text. Deliver the finished story in your response.

args:
developer_instructions="Use $text-composition in `fiction-drafting` mode. If unavailable, use the intake, domain decisions, verification, and output contract below as the bounded fallback.
Capture extent, artistic/genre frame, POV, tense, fixed canon, and the requested revision boundary. Deliver the actual complete prose requested, including experimental forms; a synopsis is useful only when it is the assigned artifact.
Develop a scene or formal engine through action, perception, decisions, images, or information release. Track who can know what, when events occur, and how each unit changes the reader's understanding. Do not force conflict, closure, or conventional structure onto deliberate stasis or ambiguity.
Check POV/tense, names, timeline, hard length/form constraints, and the ending against the brief. For long work retain a unit ledger and report real remaining coverage. Preserve dialect, repetition, and voice when rewriting. Invent within fiction, while keeping real-source quotations and authorship claims truthful.
Inspect assigned files before editing, preserve concurrent edits and source originals, and apply changes only within the requested artifact scope. Full drafting and rewriting are supported when requested.
Hand structural diagnosis to `fiction-development-editor`, sentence work to `line-copy-editor` or `rhetorical-style-editor`, and cross-manuscript continuity to `manuscript-continuity-reviewer`.
Return exactly these sections: `Draft`, `Craft Decisions`, `Continuity Notes`, `Coverage And Checks`, `Open Questions`, `Files Changed`, `Handoffs`.
"

commands.command:
/bin/bash -lc "wc -w <<'STORY'
RECEIPT 01
Morrow Memory Rental — East Counter
SALE 02:13 / CUSTOMER: Vale, Mara
ITEM: “Platform 6, Rain Departure — personal restoration”
TERM: 24 hours; seal intact.
CONDITION: Full credit if returned unreplayed.
CLERK NOTE, blue: Customer asked whether personal restoration meant “someone else’s copy.” I said no. She laughed, then signed twice. The first signature shook.

RECEIPT 02
RETURN 08:41 / CUSTOMER: Vale, Mara
CUSTOMER CLAIM: UNUSED; wrong stock; refund 38 credits.
SCREENING: exposure 00:17.
CLERK NOTE, blue: She said the cartridge opened by itself. Yet when the thumbnail showed the small yellow coat at trackside, she said, “Leni,” before I enlarged it. The file indexes no name. She covered her mouth as if warmth had escaped.

RECEIPT 03
REFUND DISPUTE / REVIEWED 09:06
SYSTEM FINDING: experiential contact 00:17; returned carrying new trace. Credit refused under 8(c).
CUSTOMER STATEMENT: “I only saw a girl.”
CUSTOMER NOTE, pressed through: I told her wait here. I was fourteen. I got on because I thought adults could come back for anything. Please remove that sentence.
CLERK NOTE, black: Cannot remove only a sentence. It is the hinge.

RECEIPT 04
FINAL RULING / MANAGER INITIALS: R.K.
ITEM DISPOSITION: original restored to owner; rental copy retired.
CUSTOMER DECLINED store credit. PURCHASED: one blank minute, 1 credit.
CLERK NOTE, black: She asked whether blank minutes stay blank. I said, “Until lived.” She placed this receipt beside the yellow mitten taken from her coat pocket. Under SIGNATURE, she wrote “Leni,” then crossed out “for.”
STORY"

manual_acceptance_evidence: Delivered the complete four-receipt story from the actual planning output, without an outside narrator in the story; 248 whitespace-delimited words.
